get.summary: Owner only: accounts with role and sign-in source (no password data).

post.summary: Owner only: add an admin or guest account with a password.

delete.summary: Owner only: remove an account (not the owner); its sessions end.

get.summary: Sources that need a person (verification, sign-in): open items with the next automatic retry.

post.summary: Check an assistance item again now (in the background).
Sign in with name and password (login page). Failed attempts slow down and are logged.
Sign out. Ends every session of the account, on all devices.

get.summary: Who is calling: name, role and how they signed in.

post.summary: Change your own password; other sessions of the account end.
First boot: create the owner account (the first admin) and sign in. Refused once an owner exists.

get.summary: Sign-in method, whether the owner account still has to be created, and who is signed in.
The running values the UI needs to describe this instance.
PERF-9: all logs and diagnostics in one download, with secrets and private data removed.
Timing samples per work phase (no URLs, titles or keys).

post.summary: Check which API features the source or main engine answers (target: source or main) and save the report.

get.summary: Recent errors grouped by cause with counts, newest first (resolved ones included).

post.summary: Remove resolved errors (or all errors with resolved_only=false).

get.summary: Status page: version, databases, catalogue counts, active errors and dependency checks.
Job queue: workers, running and queued jobs with ETA, and per-type run limit, average time, failures and freezes.
Keys page: the automatic admin token, the permanent admin key, reader keys (one per device) and script keys.

post.summary: Create a key (kind admin, reader or script; scripts are admin or guest). The secret is shown only in this answer.
Owner only: replace the automatic admin token; the old one stops working at once.

delete.summary: Revoke a key at once (a lost phone is cut off without touching other devices).

get.summary: Security log: sign-ins, failed sign-ins, slow-downs, key, token and account events, newest first; filter with ?kind=.
Effective settings grouped as on the Settings page; secret values are hidden.

put.summary: Save changed settings to config.json. Null resets a setting to its default; an empty secret removes it.

get.summary: What this start converted from autosourcarr.env to config.json.
The settings schema: name, type, default, description, secret, Compose variable and wizard step.
What the last update changed in your settings, until dismissed.

post.summary: Hide the update notice.

get.summary: Setup wizard fields with the current values; secrets show only whether one is saved.

post.summary: Save the wizard's changes to config.json in one step; a repeated request id returns the first result.
Check draft reader addresses and key without saving them.
Restart the integrated image to apply saved settings.

get.summary: Source browser identity (user-agent preset and value), presets, the identity the engine uses now and the WebView state.

post.summary: Remove the engine's cookies and browser data (sign-ins and Cloudflare clearances). Installed extensions stay.
Apply the saved repositories and load every installed extension again (new headers, changed settings). Installed extensions and sign-ins stay.

put.summary: Save the source browser identity and apply it to the running engine (sources rebuild their headers).

get.summary: Source engine status: mode, state, readiness, restarts, last error and the Cloudflare handlers (WebView, FlareSolverr).

post.summary: Report the Cloudflare handlers now. The source host solves challenges when a source meets one; queued is true when a handler is ready.

get.summary: Installed and available extensions from the configured repositories (?refresh=true reloads the repositories).

post.summary: Update every installed extension that has a newer version.

Check a source APK (archive structure, manifest and entry point, no native code) and list its permissions, web addresses and warnings; nothing is installed. The file waits 10 minutes for POST /source-extensions/upload/confirm with its sha256.
Install a source APK checked by POST /source-extensions/upload (body: sha256) within 10 minutes of its check.
Install, update or uninstall an extension; the source list refreshes in the background.
Create a source group (members share one priority; the member with the most chapters serves).

delete.summary: Delete a source group; its members become ungrouped.

put.summary: Rename a source group or change its priority.

get.summary: Source repair status: worker configuration, the daily check switch and the last repair promotion and which repair kinds can run.
Last automatic repair pass and the attempts per package.

post.summary: Start an automatic repair pass of moved sources now (REP-6).

get.summary: Where repairs run: always inside this instance (no external worker); which repair kinds are available.

put.summary: Retired: external repair worker connections were removed (410).

get.summary: In-app repair state: domain repair availability, whether a repair is running, AI provider (not configured until Connections) and the runner check.

post.summary: Repair control actions: check (or prepare) runs the repair runner self-check; account actions answer 409 until an AI provider is configured.

get.summary: Retired: the repair host-policy bundle was removed with the external worker (410).
Installed source extensions with their package, version, repository and source identities.

post.summary: Start a domain-move repair of an installed source (body: pkg_name, optional new_host, old_host, query, https) as a job; answers the job's task id.

get.summary: A repair job: its task (state, progress, message) and the matching repair report (migration, structure and content checks, rollback).

post.summary: Cancel a queued or running repair job; a repair that already changed the source rolls back itself.

get.summary: Download the repaired jar a domain repair installed (kept copy, or the installed jar when its digest still matches); 404 otherwise.

post.summary: Discard a repair: when it installed a repaired jar, the jar kept before it is installed again (a rollback job); otherwise nothing changes.
Feedback on the current installed repair (action fixed, retry or revert; installed_sha256 must match). Kept in feedback.jsonl (bounded); revert queues a rollback.

get.summary: Download the working jar that was kept before the repair (a JAR is a ZIP).

post.summary: Domain repairs install themselves: for a repaired job this answers 200 with its report and changes nothing; otherwise 409.
Keep the original APK of an installed source as repair evidence (headers confirm the original and its version).

get.summary: The repair AI provider; answers state not-configured until AI providers arrive with Connections.

post.summary: Test the repair AI provider (409 while none is configured).

get.summary: Raw-code state of an installed source (needs-input, acquiring, available, reconstructing); adopts retained repair code that matches the installed binary.
Download the retained source code of an installed source as a portable ZIP.

post.summary: Look up the source's repository in the configured indexes (body: revision); runs in the background.
Fetch the source code from its original public repository (body: revision, origin {repository, module, revision, ecosystem}).
Upload the source project ZIP of an installed source (headers X-Raw-Revision, X-Source-Version, optional X-Source-Module; at most 32 MiB). Kept private.
Ask for new source code input again (body: revision).
The code is unavailable: rebuild the source from its installed binary (body: revision, optional job_id). Needs an AI provider; 409 until Connections.
Install the working jar kept before the last repair of a package again, as a job (body pkg_name; without a body, the package of the last installed repair record).
Retired: Compose/SSH repair worker setup was removed (410).

put.summary: Turn automatic repair of moved sources on or off (domain repairs need no worker).

get.summary: Details of one title as its source reports them (refreshed from the source).
Orphaned sources under two headers, Installed and Not installed, each with its own orphan group (SRC-3); items lists them all, with discovery and installation state.

post.summary: Collect removed sources from sampled original Keiyoushi history (two years) in the background; at most once a minute.
Install the original archived package of a removed source (digest and package identity checked; never replaces an installed source).
Mark an installed source as orphaned (only when it is missing from the configured repositories).
Repair an installed orphan by moving it to its new web address (forwards to /api/v1/source-repairs/{pkgName}/domain).
Return an installed orphan to the Installed list.

get.summary: The last repair or rollback report of a package (state repaired, refused, failed, rolled_back or rollback_failed, with the migration, structure and content checks).

post.summary: Repair an installed source whose website moved: keep its jar, rewrite the old host in its compiled strings (new_host, or the observed redirect), check the structure, install, check content, and roll back when the check fails. Runs as a job.
Install the last kept working jar of a package again (as a job).

get.summary: Available sources with enabled, priority, group and language choices, and the source groups.

post.summary: Read the installed sources from the engine and store them (new sources get the default choices; empty engine lists keep existing ones).

put.summary: Change a source's choices: enabled, priority, group, official, matching rules.

get.summary: The extension's own settings for this source (as in Mihon), with current values.

put.summary: Change one extension setting of this source.

get.summary: Catalogue, chapter, source, cache and storage counts; refreshed at most every 15 seconds.
Where the databases are and how large they are.

post.summary: Copy, check and switch both databases to another mounted folder (SET-5); the old files are kept.

get.summary: Main Suwayomi library entries from the AutoSourcarr source, mapped to catalogue entries: entry_ids, items, stats_by_entry (chapter and downloaded counts), ok and error.

Ongoing, completed and failed tasks with progress, ETA and finish time; job type, priority and queue position for queued work; repair jobs are listed as kind source-repair with package and repair state.

post.summary: Remove completed and failed tasks from the list; running and queued work stays.
Cancel a queued or running task. Work already done stays; the task is listed as failed with "Cancelled by user".
Replay an interrupted task only when replaying it cannot change data twice (read-only observations).
